title: Four Noble Truths and the Eightfold Path
welcome_lead: Approach the heart of the Buddha's teaching: the diagnosis of suffering and its cure.
meta_desc: IBDP Religious Studies Adventure: Four Noble Truths and the Noble Eightfold Path.
final_note: You have followed the Buddha's medical analysis of human life. The path remains open to practice.

concepts.def: Buddha's diagnosis: suffering exists, has a cause, can cease and there is a path to its cessation.
Suffering, unsatisfactoriness or unease that pervades unawakened life.
Craving or thirst that gives rise to dukkha.
Cessation of craving and suffering; the goal of Buddhist practice.
Eight interrelated factors leading to liberation, grouped under wisdom, ethics and concentration.

walkthroughs.body_html: The Buddha's first sermon at Sarnath taught the Four Noble Truths: (1) dukkha; (2) its origin in craving; (3) its cessation; (4) the path. This medical pattern frames suffering as a problem to be addressed practically.

The Noble Eightfold Path lists right view, right intention (wisdom); right speech, right action, right livelihood (ethics); right effort, right mindfulness, right concentration (mental discipline). The path is interdependent rather than sequential.

The Three Marks describe conditioned reality: anicca, the impermanence of all phenomena; anatta, the absence of an unchanging self; dukkha, the resulting unease. Insight into these marks underpins liberation.
